paragraph: Montvale's single-family market is the core of the activity, with 20 sales over six months at a median of $1,282,000, mostly four-bedroom colonials with a couple of baths and a few bi-levels and split-levels mixed in. A sale-to-list ratio of 1.04, 70 percent of homes closing above asking, and a median of 16 days on market put this squarely in seller's territory, and buyers should expect competition on the good ones. Sales ran from $700,000 to $2,800,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. Townhouses and condos are a real second tier here, 14 sales at a median of $876,000, and the category leans toward townhouses rather than flats, typically two bedrooms and two baths. Competition exists there too, with roughly two thirds closing above asking, though a median of 22.5 days on market makes it competitive rather than frenzied. Monthly counts are too thin to read a trend from any single month, and while July shows more single-family closings at a lower median, that reads as a mix shift toward the entry end, not falling values. If you're choosing between tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance lifestyle of a townhouse.
